title: ACE Code of Ethics for ACE Certified Professionals
why: Nine binding promises: safety, boundaries, confidentiality, referral. Full text on page.

title: ACE Personal Trainer Manual 5th ed, Chapter 1: Role and Scope of Practice
why: Canonical scope-of-practice chapter; 72 scope mentions, defines the trainer boundary.

title: NASM Code of Professional Conduct
why: Prevention-only scope, no diagnosis, mandatory health-history screening before training.

title: NSCA Codes, Policies and Procedures (Professional Code of Ethics, 2024 revision)
why: Full NSCA Code of Ethics text; supersedes all earlier NSCA ethics documents.

title: NSCA Strength and Conditioning Professional Standards and Guidelines
why: Duty-of-care standards: screening, supervision, records, emergency planning, facility rules.

title: ACSM Code of Ethics
why: ACSM member and certificant conduct rules; the medical-adjacent ethics baseline.

title: CIMSPA Professional Standard: Personal Trainer (full standard) v1.1
why: UK occupational standard; competences, professional code of conduct, hands-on-contact rules.

title: IDEA Code of Ethics for Personal Trainers
why: Trade-body ethics list; weakest authority here but explicitly in scope.

title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) consolidated text, Article 50
why: Binding AI transparency duty: users must be told they interact with AI.

title: ACSM CEO Update Q3 2025 (AI in exercise science position)
why: Nearest thing to an ACSM organizational statement on AI coaching.

title: Michie et al. 2013, Behavior Change Technique Taxonomy v1 (93 techniques)
why: Author-accepted full text of BCTTv1; the standard vocabulary for coaching techniques.

title: Teixeira et al. 2012, Exercise, physical activity, and self-determination theory
why: Systematic review linking autonomy support to exercise adherence; SDT applied to exercise.

title: Gardner, Lally & Wardle 2012, Making health habitual (BJGP)
why: Habit-formation review; the practitioner-facing synthesis of repetition and cue consistency.

title: Samdal et al. 2017, Effective BCTs for physical activity and healthy eating
why: Meta-regression of which BCTs actually move adherence in overweight adults.

title: Wulf 2013, Attentional focus and motor learning: a review of 15 years
why: Evidence base for external-focus cueing; author-hosted full text of the review.

title: Deci & Ryan 2000, The what and why of goal pursuits (Psychological Inquiry)
why: Core SDT statement of autonomy, competence, relatedness that Teixeira applies.

title: Ryan & Deci 2000, Self-determination theory and facilitation of intrinsic motivation
why: The canonical SDT overview paper underpinning the exercise review.

title: Markland, Ryan, Tobin & Rollnick 2005, Motivational interviewing and self-determination theory
why: Bridges MI practice to SDT mechanism; heavily cited by Teixeira.

title: MINT, Understanding Motivational Interviewing (Miller & Rollnick definition)
why: Miller and Rollnick's own body's definition of MI spirit and processes.

title: Lally et al. 2010, How are habits formed: modelling habit formation in the real world
why: Source of the 66-day median habit-formation figure Gardner reports.

title: Wood & Neal 2007, A new look at habits and the habit-goal interface
why: Habit-as-cue-response theory Gardner builds the practitioner advice on.

title: Bandura 2001, Social cognitive theory: an agentic perspective
why: The Bandura reference Gardner actually cites for agency and self-efficacy.

title: Michie et al. 2009, Effective techniques in healthy eating and physical activity interventions
why: Self-monitoring plus control-theory techniques meta-regression; BCTTv1 reference 14.

title: Michie, van Stralen & West 2011, The Behaviour Change Wheel
why: COM-B framework for choosing interventions; BCTTv1 reference 48.

title: Wulf, Hoss & Prinz 1998, Instructions for motor learning: internal versus external focus
why: The founding external-focus experiments the 2013 review is built around.

title: McNevin, Shea & Wulf 2003, Increasing the distance of an external focus of attention
why: Distance effect for cue placement; most-cited supporting study in the review.

title: European Commission FAQ, Transparency obligations under Article 50 AI Act
why: Official Commission reading of Article 50; fetchable where eur-lex is not.

title: Prochaska & Velicer 1997, The transtheoretical model of health behavior change
why: Brief-named TTM primary; demoted by the fifteen-primary cap.

title: Prochaska & DiClemente 1983, Stages and processes of self-change of smoking
why: Original stages-of-change paper; no verified citing primary in this set.

title: Bandura 1977, Self-efficacy: toward a unifying theory of behavioral change
why: Brief-named self-efficacy primary; no primary here cites this 1977 paper.

title: Gollwitzer 1999, Implementation intentions: strong effects of simple plans
why: If-then planning primary; no verified citing primary in this set.

title: ACSM 2009 position stand, Progression models in resistance training for healthy adults
why: Nearest authoritative source for realistic rate-of-gain expectations.

title: Riebe et al. 2015, Updating ACSM's exercise preparticipation health screening
why: Decides who needs medical clearance before training; underpins the referral rule.
